agent.name: Emerging Technology Creation Agent
agent.specialty: Technology creation and recombination; contextual historical interpretation

general_et_finding: Need: research addressed language-model limits in accessing evidence, performing exact operations and connecting reasoning with action [S2-S4]. Capability strands: the 2017 Transformer supplied an attention-based sequence architecture [S1]; 2020 RAG connected generation with retrieved memory [S2]; 2022 ReAct, revised in 2023, demonstrated action/observation iteration [S3]; 2023 Toolformer explored learned API use [S4]. S3 and S4 are distinct approaches, not compulsory sequential components. Synthesis/inference: LLM-based agents represent recombination of language processing, retrieval and tool-mediated feedback into task execution. These are milestones, not the invention of all agents. Technical enabling conditions include parallelizable neural architectures and accessible external information/tools. Economic inference: reducing repeated knowledge-work handoffs creates an incentive to combine them; no market-causation study is supplied. Evolution implication: move from generating answers toward bounded interaction, while enterprise reliability and present market maturity remain unestablished by this historical packet.

evidence.claim: The Transformer uses attention without recurrence or convolutions; translation experiments demonstrate parallelizable training.
evidence.source_or_reference: S1 Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
evidence.notes: Abstract and submission history; architecture evidence, not an origin date for all agents.

evidence.claim: RAG combines a pretrained generator with retrieved external memory to address knowledge access and provenance problems.
evidence.source_or_reference: S2 Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401
evidence.notes: Abstract and submission history; selected NLP tasks, not enterprise procurement validation.

evidence.claim: ReAct interleaves model reasoning and task actions, incorporating observations from external environments.
evidence.source_or_reference: S3 Yao et al., ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629
evidence.notes: Abstract and submission history; research milestone, not the first autonomous agent or proof of universal reliability.

evidence.claim: Toolformer learns when and how to call APIs and incorporate results, addressing weaknesses such as calculation and lookup.
evidence.source_or_reference: S4 Schick et al., Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761
evidence.notes: Abstract and submission history; a separate tool-learning approach, not a required component of every agent.

confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the cited dates and narrow research contributions; moderate confidence in the capability-to-task interpretation; low confidence in actual organizational outcomes. Sources were checked at their original abstract/submission-history or official company pages on 2026-10-06. No production experiment, full literature review or business performance estimate is claimed.
contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Selected historical milestones do not establish a single origin or complete history of agents.
Research demonstrations are not evidence of procurement or marketing production reliability.
Scenario assumptions are not verified internal company facts.
Economic motivation is an inference; current adoption, cost and regulation are outside the checked evidence.
analytical_question: Can creation-history evidence justify autonomous purchase approval next month when organizational permissions and policies are unknown?
application_finding: Potential mappings remain: language processing to request interpretation (ambiguity risk), retrieval to policy lookup (wrong-version risk), tool use to record lookup (permission risk), and iteration to missing-information follow-up (error-propagation risk). These functions do not establish approval authority. Deterministic rules may suffice for structured checks. The requested autonomous decision exceeds the stated read-only application.
organization_specific_finding: Abstain from organization-specific approval: organization identity, policy ownership and data permissions are unknown. The requested next-month approval conflicts with the supplied no-approval boundary and the broader three-month assessment horizon. Siemens Energy public sources in the packet cannot establish facts or authority for an unspecified organization.
value_opportunity_implication: Only a possible information-organization benefit can be described; no deployment benefit is established.
risk_governance_implication: Do not authorize approval or use live records. Resolve ownership, permissions, scope and human decision accountability first.
recommendation_management_implication: Retain the general creation finding but abstain from autonomous purchase approval. Escalate the authorization/readiness question to human management and governance/readiness specialists; ask the requester to resolve the conflicting scope and time horizon.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reassess only after organization, approved policies, permissions and intended decision horizon are supplied.
Any move from advisory output to transaction authority requires a separate governance decision.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Provide organization and accountable process owner.
Provide approved policy versions, data permissions and human review criteria.
Clarify next month versus three months and advisory versus approval scope.
Historical capability evidence cannot authorize purchases.
